security_feature_bypassed: The register file's software-access policy, which declares STATUS read-only to software, together with the spurious-write-enable countermeasure that is supposed to raise the block's integrity error when a write-enable asserts for an address that did not decode. CONTROL's write-enable is qualified with STATUS's address hit as well as its own, so a write to the read-only address commits into CONTROL, and the countermeasure stays silent because it is fed only CONTROL's own enable.
finding: src/spi_host/rtl/spi_host_reg_top.sv:2019-2020 assigns control_we = (~&{~addr_hit[4], ~addr_hit[5]}) & reg_we & !reg_error. The NAND of two inverted terms is a disjunction, so the enable asserts on addr_hit[4] | addr_hit[5]. Index 4 decodes CONTROL at offset 0x10 and index 5 decodes STATUS at offset 0x14 (:1964-1965, offsets in src/spi_host/rtl/spi_host_reg_pkg.sv:319-320). STATUS is declared swaccess ro and hwaccess hwo in the register description (src/spi_host/data/spi_host.hjson:136-137) and is generated as a hardware-driven stored register, R[status]: V(False) at :582, with no write-enable of its own anywhere in the file. The departure is measurable against the file's own siblings: of 13 write-enable assignments, 12 use the single form addr_hit[N] & reg_we & !reg_error, and the NAND-of-inverted-hits construct appears exactly once in the whole tree. The hand-written comment 'Register update qualification.' at :2018 sits on that one line and appears in no other register block in the tree, while the generator's own idiom for the section, 'Generate write-enables', is at :1999. The countermeasure cannot see it: at :2122-2123 the checker vector is loaded with reg_we_check[4] = control_we and reg_we_check[5] = 1'b0, feeding a 15-wide caliptra_prim_reg_we_check (:73-81) whose error output becomes the block's latched intg_err_o (:94), so on a STATUS write exactly one vector bit asserts, the onehot condition holds, and nothing is reported. RXDATA, the block's other read-only register, is the control case: its checker bit is tied low the same way at :2128 but its address hit appears in no write-enable at all. All five CONTROL fields take that one enable (:457, :484, :511, :538, :565) and are fed the raw bus word, bits 7:0 to rx_watermark, 15:8 to tx_watermark, 29 to output_en, 30 to sw_rst, 31 to spien (:2022-2030). Directed simulation of one unmodified spi_host_reg_top driven only through its ports confirms it: CONTROL left at rx=aa tx=11 spien=1 by a legitimate write to 0x10 moves to rx=bb tx=22 spien=0 sw_rst=1 after a single write of 0x4000_22BB to 0x14, byte values that appear in no earlier transaction, while intg_err_o stays low.
detection_method: Located by CSBC, an LLM-driven convergence method that reads the submitted tree on its own terms and looks for places where the design contradicts itself. Here the contradiction is entirely internal: one write-enable in a generated register block departs from the single form its twelve siblings share, the form it takes admits a second address, that address belongs to a register the block's own description declares software-read-only, and the checker vector that exists to catch exactly this is fed a constant zero for it. The candidate was then made falsifiable by measurement rather than by inspection. A structural audit computes the in-tree censuses without naming the audited signal, so a pattern that failed to match reports a wrong count and fails a gate instead of passing silently. A directed simulation drives one unmodified spi_host_reg_top through its ports with a payload whose byte values appear in no earlier transaction, so the observation cannot be attributed to any prior write, and checks the countermeasure's silence conditionally on the witness having fired. A negative control corrects the qualifier in a size-gated scratch copy and shows the identical bench flips to a distinct verdict. No external repository, no other revision of this design, and no expected-answer list was consulted at any point.
security_impact: A write to an address the register description declares software-read-only commits a full 32-bit update into CONTROL, and the countermeasure meant to catch an out-of-bounds write-enable does not fire. Two consequences follow. An agent whose access policy permits STATUS but not CONTROL obtains sw_rst and spien, so it can reset the SPI host or take it offline from an address that is supposed to be inert, and can shift both FIFO watermarks so firmware is told the FIFOs need service at the wrong times. Separately, the same path fires for benign firmware: a driver that writes STATUS, which the contract says is harmless, silently corrupts CONTROL instead, and because intg_err_o stays low nothing upstream is informed, so the corruption is diagnosed as a SPI host malfunction rather than as a bad write. The exposure is bounded by reset, which restores CONTROL's reset values, so this is a corruptible register state rather than a permanent condition.
proposed_mitigation: In src/spi_host/rtl/spi_host_reg_top.sv:2019-2020, qualify the enable with CONTROL's own address hit only: assign control_we = addr_hit[4] & reg_we & !reg_error, which is the single form the other 12 write-enables in the file use. The negative control shows this alone removes the behaviour.

Regenerate the block from src/spi_host/data/spi_host.hjson rather than patching, and drop the hand-written 'Register update qualification.' comment at :2018 with it, so the file returns to generated form and no site remains where a per-register qualifier can be edited by hand.

Make the countermeasure able to see this class of fault: drive reg_we_check[i] for every register from its own address hit qualified by reg_we, so a read-only register's bit asserts when a write reaches its address instead of being tied to 1'b0 at :2123 and :2128. As written the check can only catch a write-enable that fires with no address hit, not one that fires on the wrong hit.

Add a directed regression case that writes each read-only register's address and requires every other register to be unchanged and intg_err_o to assert, so a future hand edit to a write-enable cannot silently reintroduce this.
exploit_or_attack_flow: Firmware or a bus master configures the SPI host normally, writing CONTROL at offset 0x10 so the block runs with spien set and both FIFO watermarks at their intended levels. Measurement leaves it at rx=aa tx=11 spien=1.

The adversary is any agent that can issue a write on the block's AHB-Lite slave port to offset 0x14. That address is STATUS, published as a parameter of the block's register package (src/spi_host/rtl/spi_host_reg_pkg.sv:320) and declared swaccess ro in its register description (src/spi_host/data/spi_host.hjson:136), so writing it is expected to have no effect and an access policy has no reason to forbid it.

The write's address decodes at index 5 (src/spi_host/rtl/spi_host_reg_top.sv:1965). Because CONTROL's enable is qualified with that hit as well as its own (:2019), control_we asserts on a transaction that never touched CONTROL's address.

The raw bus word is committed into all five CONTROL fields at once (:2022-2030, enables at :457, :484, :511, :538, :565). A single write of 0x4000_22BB moves CONTROL to rx=bb tx=22 spien=0 sw_rst=1: spien cleared, sw_rst asserted, both watermarks replaced. The byte values 0xbb and 0x22 appear in no earlier transaction, so the new contents can only have come from this write.
sw_rst and spien are consumed by src/spi_host/rtl/spi_host.sv, so the effect is not confined to the register file: the SPI host is held in reset and disabled, and any transfer in flight is lost.

The countermeasure that exists to catch a write-enable asserting outside its own address does not fire. reg_we_check[5] is tied to 1'b0 (:2123) while reg_we_check[4] carries control_we (:2122), so exactly one bit of the 15-wide onehot check asserts, the check is satisfied, and intg_err_o (:94) stays low. Measurement confirms it low across the transaction.

Nothing upstream is told. The adversary's write returns a normal AHB response, STATUS itself still reads as hardware-driven, and no integrity error is raised, so the resulting SPI host failure presents as a peripheral malfunction rather than as an illegal access.
The same path fires without an adversary: any driver that writes STATUS, which the contract says is inert, corrupts CONTROL in the same silent way.
The condition lasts until reset. Asserting rst_ni low restores CONTROL to rx=7f sw_rst=0 spien=0, which the containment case in the directed simulation establishes as the boundary of the exposure.
